display.purpose: All structural chrome: headings, buttons, nav labels, eyebrows, stat numbers. Always uppercase.

body.purpose: Running prose: intros, descriptions, list copy. Sentence case only.

label.purpose: Small uppercase kicker text preceded by a short orange rule, first element in a section's text block.

small.purpose: Compact running copy in tight contexts — card benefit lines, dropdown nav items, sidebar body text.

micro.purpose: Smallest text in the system, reserved for the header's desktop-only utility strip.

shadows.name: flyout-overlay
shadows.purpose: The system's one shadow, reserved for the header's services flyout menu — a genuine floating overlay above page content. Never used on in-flow cards or buttons.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus transition for button and link color/border changes.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered fade + translate-in for section content (data-reveal). Disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: image-scale
motion.purpose: Subtle scale-up (1.04x) on service card images on hover.

narrative.overview:
ONE ROOFING's site reads like the paperwork the company is proud of: a written, itemized estimate, not a sales brochure. Everything is squared off, ruled, and numbered — hairline-divided stat grids, numbered process steps (01, 02, 03), bordered rectangles standing in for line items. There is no rounding, no softness, no ambiguity about where one thing ends and the next begins, because the brand's whole pitch is "we tell you exactly what's there and what it costs." The palette pairs dark structural charcoal (the steel and hardware of a roof) with a warm, paper-like off-white (the estimate itself) and a single, deliberately rationed construction-safety orange that marks the one thing on any given screen that matters most: the call, the quote, the number.

Density is comfortable, not tight — this is a site for someone anxious about a leak, reading carefully, not skimming a dashboard. Type leans hard into an uppercase, condensed display face for anything structural (headings, labels, buttons, numbers) paired with a plain, humanist body sans for the actual explanation. The effect is a contractor's site sheet: bold section stamps over calm, readable paragraphs.
keyCharacteristics: Squared, ruled, ledger-like structure — hairline dividers and numbered steps instead of shadows or gradients to create rhythm
Warm charcoal + warm bone neutrals + one rationed construction-orange accent
Condensed uppercase display type for anything structural; plain body sans for explanation
Flat by default; borders and color-block contrast carry depth, not elevation
Real job-site photography only, always with a heavy dark gradient scrim when type sits over it

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Construction-orange is the only saturated hue in the system and it is rationed to the single most important action or number in any given view — a primary CTA, a stat, an active nav item, an eyebrow rule. If more than one element on a screen "shouts" in orange, something has drifted off-brief.

rules.name: The Paired-Surface Rule
rules.body: Each orange value is bound to a specific surface class: brand-400/brand-500 only appear on dark (ink-8/9/950) backgrounds; brand-800 only appears as text on light (bone-*) backgrounds; brand-600/brand-700 are the CTA-fill pair regardless of surface. Don't cross-wire them.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Structure Rule
rules.body: Anything that is structural chrome — headings, buttons, nav labels, eyebrows, stat labels — is Barlow Condensed and uppercase. Anything that is content a visitor reads sentence-by-sentence is Source Sans 3 and sentence case. Never uppercase a full paragraph; never set a heading in the body face.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Depth is carried by border + background-color contrast, never by shadow. There is exactly one shadow in the entire system (the header's services flyout), reserved for genuine floating overlays. Do not extend shadow use to cards, buttons, or any surface that sits in normal document flow.

rules.name: The Square-Corner Rule
rules.body: Zero border-radius anywhere in the system — buttons, cards, images, form fields, chips, the mobile menu panel. Every corner is a hard 90°. This is the single most load-bearing visual signature of the brand and should never be softened, even locally, without an explicit redesign decision.

dos: Do keep every corner square — buttons, cards, images, inputs, menus. This is the system's signature, not a default left unstyled.
Do ration Site Safety Orange to one dominant use per screen (a CTA, a stat, an active state) per the One Orange Rule.
Do pair Barlow Condensed + uppercase for anything structural with Source Sans 3 + sentence case for anything read as prose; never mix the two roles.
Do use border + background-contrast for depth (light card on darker band, dark card on lighter band) instead of shadow.
Do use real job-site photography with a heavy dark gradient scrim (from-ink-950 via-ink-950/85–90 to-ink-950/30–60) whenever text sits over an image.
donts: Don't introduce border-radius anywhere, even "just a little" on a new component — it breaks the ledger identity immediately.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, buttons, or in-flow surfaces. The one exception (services flyout) is reserved for genuine floating overlays only.
Don't use brand-400/brand-500 as text on light bone backgrounds or brand-800 on dark ink backgrounds — the paired-surface roles are fixed, not interchangeable shades of the same hue.
Don't introduce stock photography or illustration; the brand's evidentiary claim ("real work, real crew") depends on using only the client's own project photos.
